speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

The clinical picture of a new, subacute headache and progressive vision loss in a 69-year-old, combined with the urgency of potential optic nerve or retinal artery involvement, strongly suggests vasculitis of the cranial arteries. Given the risk of permanent blindness, this is a medical emergency requiring immediate initiation of high-dose corticosteroids and confirmation via temporal artery biopsy.
